overview.text: This entry shows Christ Anapeson, the reclining Christ, in the Dionysiou Monastery fresco. The catalogue identifies a sixteenth-century work on Mount Athos. The title is kept distinct here from every later Russian composition called the Unsleeping Eye.

blocks.text: Christ reclines as a child in the centre, attended by the Mother of God and an angelic figure. The displayed composition belongs to the fresco identified by its source as Anapeson at Dionysiou, rather than an illustration of a particular Gospel verse.

blocks.text: Archpriest David Lesko discusses a related Russian Unsleeping Eye composition as an image of Christ’s protective vigilance, first appearing there around the end of the fifteenth century. He connects its symbolism with the lion of Judah, but explicitly distinguishes the Slumber of the Christ Child from the Unsleeping Eye in footnote 2. These titles therefore cannot be treated as exact synonyms for all variants.
